To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stomatal closure in maize is caused by the decrease in soil hydraulic conductivity during soil drying.

the soil-root system has a nonlinear hydraulic conductance and that the stomata of maize plants respond to the nonlinearities in the soil-root conductance to maintain linearity between transpiration and xylem tension.

the relationship between leaf xylem water potential and transpitation rate in maize plants is nonlinear at soil drying, and that stomata close in response to the loss of hydraulic conductance in a predictable way, maintaining the lineairity between xylem water potencial and transpiration rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of soil water deficit on the hydraulic conductance of the soil-root-xylem continuum and on the regulation of stomata in maize.
the relationship between transpirational water loss and soil water availability.
the effect of soil and plant hydromechanics on stomatal regulation during soil drying.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stomatal closure during soil drying maintains the linearity in the relationship leaf water potential and stomatal conductance.

stomatal closure is a consequence of the loss of soil- plant hydraulic conductance, but stomatal closure is also an active process that maintains the soil-plant system in a linear relationship between transpiration, and leaf water potential, avoiding a further loss of soil hydraulic capacity.
stomata regulation is not a mechanism to maintain soil-plant hydraulic conductivity, but a mechanism to avoid the loss of soil- plant hydraulic conductance in soils with low hydraulic conductivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of soil- plant hydraulic conductivity is the main driver of stomatal closure in drying soil.
stomata regulation avoids a loss in soil-plant hydraulic conductivity in drying soil.
the stomata of maize plants close to maintain the soil-plant water potential gradient and avoid the loss of soil- plant hydraulic conductance during soil drying.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stomata regulation in response to soil drying is not a random process but a mechanism that avoids a loss of plant hydraulic conductance.
stomata closure in drying soils is a hydraulic response to maintain the hydraulic conductance of the soil-plant system.
stomatal regulation avoids the loss of soil-Plant hydraulic conductance in soils with a high water content.
